import json
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

data = json.loads('{"person": {"name": "Ada", "age": 36}}')
root = ET.Element("person")
for key, value in data["person"].items():
    child = ET.SubElement(root, key)
    child.text = str(value)
ET.ElementTree(root).write("person.xml", encoding="unicode", xml_declaration=True)

instruction:
Convert this XML document to JSON:

<user id="7">
  <name>Grace</name>
  <role>admin</role>
</user>
output:
import json
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

root = ET.fromstring('<user id="7"><name>Grace</name><role>admin</role></user>')
obj = {"@id": root.get("id")}
for child in root:
    obj[child.tag] = child.text
print(json.dumps({root.tag: obj}, indent=2))

root = ET.Element("product", {"sku": product["@sku"]})

instruction:
Convert this nested XML with repeated tags to a JSON object that collects repeats into lists:

<catalog>
  <book>A</book>
  <book>B</book>
  <author>Kim</author>
</catalog>
output:
import json
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
from collections import defaultdict

root = ET.fromstring('<catalog><book>A</book><book>B</book><author>Kim</author></catalog>')
collected = defaultdict(list)
for child in root:
    collected[child.tag].append(child.text)
print(json.dumps({"catalog": dict(collected)}, indent=2))
